record.paper_title: Exact results and open questions in first principle functional RG
record.original_question: Can one develop a unified functional renormalization-group framework for strong-disorder systems that, instead of tracking only rapidly growing disorder moments associated with rare events, follows the full probability distributions that govern typical events and works beyond the few special strong-disorder examples already understood?

evidence.quote: An outstanding question is how general this is, whether other systems can be treated in that way, and whether a unified (functional) RG approach to strong disorder problems can be found.

artifact.category_tag: Functional renormalization group for disordered systems
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature continues to develop FRG techniques for disordered systems and to compute full probability distributions (e.g., critical order-parameter distributions via FRG, 2022) and SDRG approaches separately, but no single unified FRG framework that flows full probability distributions and recovers SDRG infinite-disorder fixed points across a broad class of strong-disorder systems appears to have been established. Reviews of FRG for disordered systems and SDRG primers treat the two formalisms as distinct, suggesting the unification problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Critical probability distributions of the order parameter from the functional renormalization group
status_evidence.snippet: FRG used to compute full probability distribution functions of the order parameter at criticality (3D Ising), illustrating progress on distributional FRG but in pure (non-strong-disorder) setting.
status_evidence.claim: FRG can access full distributions, but applications remain largely outside the strong-disorder/infinite-disorder regime.

status_evidence.title: Strong disorder renormalization group primer and the superfluid–insulator transition
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews SDRG decimation methodology focused on tracking dominant/rare couplings near infinite-disorder fixed points.
status_evidence.claim: SDRG literature still treats strong-disorder problems via decimation of extreme couplings, separate from FRG.

status_evidence.title: The Functional Renormalization Group Treatment of Disordered Systems, a Review
status_evidence.snippet: Review of FRG for disordered elastic systems based on renormalized disorder correlators/cumulants.
status_evidence.claim: FRG reviews of disordered systems do not encompass infinite-disorder SDRG fixed points in a unified manner.
